authoredSolutions.31: In the cumene process, isopropylbenzene (cumene) is oxidised by air at the benzylic tertiary C-H position. The tertiary benzylic radical formed is resonance stabilised, and it traps \(O_2\) to give the hydroperoxide \(C_6H_5C(CH_3)_2-O-O-H\), cumene hydroperoxide. This is the isolable intermediate. Treatment with dilute acid then triggers a 1,2-aryl migration to electron-deficient oxygen and hydrolysis, giving phenol and acetone. Option (C) is the drawn cumene hydroperoxide. Option (A) is cyclohexyl acetate, (B) is isopropoxycyclohexane (an ether) and (D) is cumene itself, none of which is the oxidation intermediate.
authoredSolutions.32: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution proceeds through an anionic Meisenheimer complex. The negative charge developed at the carbon bearing the nucleophile can be delocalised only onto positions ortho and para to it. A \(-NO_2\) group therefore accelerates the reaction strongly when it is ortho or para to the halogen, and hardly at all when it is meta. Option (A) is 2-nitrochlorobenzene (activated), (B) is 4-nitrochlorobenzene (activated), (D) is 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (doubly activated, fastest). Option (C) is 3-nitrochlorobenzene, where the nitro group is meta and cannot stabilise the intermediate by resonance, so it reacts slowest.
authoredSolutions.33: Characteristic flame colours of the s-block elements: potassium gives violet (lilac), calcium gives brick red, strontium gives crimson red and barium gives apple green. Hence A(K)-II, B(Ca)-I, C(Sr)-IV, D(Ba)-III, which is option (B).
authoredSolutions.34: The four Newman projections are conformers of n-butane about the \(C_2-C_3\) bond. Options (C) and (D) are eclipsed (front and rear bonds superimposed), and are destabilised by torsional strain; (D) is the fully eclipsed syn form with the two methyls eclipsing each other, the highest-energy conformer. Options (A) and (B) are staggered. In (A) the two methyl groups are \(60^{\circ}\) apart (gauche), so they suffer steric strain. In (B) the front methyl is at the top and the rear methyl at the bottom, i.e. a dihedral angle of \(180^{\circ}\) (anti). The anti-staggered conformer has neither torsional nor steric strain and is the most stable, so the answer is (B).
authoredSolutions.35: An enzyme-catalysed reaction follows Michaelis-Menten behaviour: rate \(= \frac{V_{max}[S]}{K_M + [S]}\). At low substrate concentration the free enzyme is plentiful, so the rate rises almost linearly with \([S]\); as \([S]\) increases the enzyme becomes saturated with substrate and the rate levels off at \(V_{max}\), independent of \([S]\). The correct plot is therefore a rising curve that flattens into a plateau, which is the third graph, labelled (C). The option that names graph (C) is option (D).
authoredSolutions.36: Acetals and ketals \(\left( R_2C(OR')_2 \right)\) are indeed stable in basic medium, so Assertion A is true. They are cleaved only under acidic conditions, where protonation of one \(-OR'\) oxygen converts it into a good leaving group \(\left( R'OH \right)\) and generates a resonance-stabilised oxocarbenium ion. In base no such protonation is possible, and the alkoxide ion \(\left( R'O^{-} \right)\) is a strongly basic, very POOR leaving group. So the stability arises from the LOW leaving tendency of alkoxide, not a high one; Reason R states the opposite and is false. Hence A is true but R is false, option (A).
authoredSolutions.37: A cube has 8 corners and 6 faces. X occupies every alternate corner, i.e. 4 corners, each shared by 8 unit cells, plus one atom at the body centre which belongs wholly to the cell: \(n_X = 4 \times \frac{1}{8} + 1 = \frac{1}{2} + 1 = 1.5\). Y occupies one third of the faces, i.e. \(\frac{6}{3} = 2\) face centres, each shared by 2 unit cells: \(n_Y = 2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1\). The formula is therefore \(X_{1.5}Y\), equivalently \(X_3Y_2\).
authoredSolutions.38: Systematic qualitative analysis separates cations by group reagent. \(Pb^{2+}\) and \(Cu^{2+}\) are group II cations, precipitated as sulphides by \(H_2S\) in the presence of dilute \(HCl\) (the common ion \(H^{+}\) suppresses ionisation of \(H_2S\), keeping \([S^{2-}]\) low enough that only the least soluble sulphides precipitate) - so A matches (i). \(Al^{3+}\) and \(Fe^{3+}\) are group III, precipitated as hydroxides by \(NH_4OH\) in the presence of \(NH_4Cl\) - B matches (iii). \(Co^{2+}\) and \(Ni^{2+}\) are group IV, precipitated as sulphides by \(H_2S\) in the presence of \(NH_4OH\), where \([S^{2-}]\) is high - C matches (iv). \(Ba^{2+}\) and \(Ca^{2+}\) are group V, precipitated as carbonates by \(\left( NH_4 \right)_2CO_3\) with \(NH_4OH\) - D matches (ii). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.39: By definition an antibiotic is a chemical substance, produced wholly or partly by metabolism of a micro-organism (or a synthetic structural analogue of such a substance), which in low concentrations INHIBITS the growth of, or destroys, micro-organisms. Statements (A), (C) and (D) all restate parts of that definition and are correct. Statement (B) says an antibiotic should promote the growth or survival of micro-organisms, which is the exact opposite of its function, so (B) is the incorrect statement.
authoredSolutions.40: In aqueous medium three effects compete: the electron-releasing inductive effect of methyl groups (raises basicity in the order \(NH_3 < MeNH_2 < Me_2NH < Me_3N\)), steric hindrance to protonation (falls in the reverse order) and solvation/hydrogen-bonding stabilisation of the conjugate acid (the more N-H bonds the ammonium ion has, the better it is hydrated, so \(MeNH_3^{+} > Me_2NH_2^{+} > Me_3NH^{+}\)). The resultant experimental order for methyl-substituted amines in water is \(Me_2NH > MeNH_2 > Me_3N > NH_3\): the secondary amine gains from the inductive effect without paying the full solvation and steric penalty, while the tertiary amine, with only one N-H bond and three bulky methyls, drops below the primary amine. This is option (B).
authoredSolutions.41: 'Volume strength' is the volume of \(O_2\) at STP liberated by unit volume of the solution: \(2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2\). So 1 L of a '25 volume' solution gives 25 L of \(O_2\) at STP. From the equation, 22.4 L of \(O_2\) at STP comes from 2 mol \(= 68\ g\) of \(H_2O_2\). Mass of \(H_2O_2\) per litre \(= \frac{68}{22.4} \times 25 = 75.9 \approx 75\ g\). Hence 1 L of the marketed solution contains about 75 g of \(H_2O_2\), option (B). (Equivalently, strength in g/L = volume strength \(\times\ 3.03\).)
authoredSolutions.42: For a one-electron species the Bohr radius is \(r_n = 0.529 \frac{n^2}{Z}\ \dot{A}\). For \(Li^{2+}\) (\(Z = 3\)) in \(n = 2\): \(x = 0.529 \times \frac{4}{3}\). For \(Be^{3+}\) (\(Z = 4\)) in \(n = 3\): \(r = 0.529 \times \frac{9}{4}\). Dividing, \(\frac{r}{x} = \frac{9/4}{4/3} = \frac{27}{16}\), so \(r = \frac{27}{16}x\), option (A).
authoredSolutions.43: White phosphorus reacts with thionyl chloride to give phosphorus trichloride: \(P_4 + 8SOCl_2 \rightarrow 4PCl_3 + 4SO_2 + 2S_2Cl_2\). So [A] is \(PCl_3\). Hydrolysis of \(PCl_3\) gives phosphorous acid: \(PCl_3 + 3H_2O \rightarrow H_3PO_3 + 3HCl\). In \(H_3PO_3\) the phosphorus bears one P-H bond and two P-OH bonds, so only two hydrogens are ionisable and the acid is DIBASIC, as the question requires. \(H_3PO_4\) would be tribasic, ruling out (B) and (C). Hence [A] \(= PCl_3\), [B] \(= H_3PO_3\), option (D).
authoredSolutions.44: Noble gases have completely filled \(ns^2np^6\) (or \(1s^2\)) configurations, so an incoming electron must enter the next higher shell; energy has to be supplied and the electron gain enthalpy is positive (endothermic). The larger the atom, the further out and less repelled that added electron is, so the positive value falls down the group. The standard values are \(He\ +48\), \(Ne\ +116\), \(Ar\ +96\), \(Kr\ +96\) and \(Xe\ +77\ kJ\ mol^{-1}\). Helium is anomalously LOW because its \(1s\) shell is so compact that the added \(2s\) electron is very weakly repelled, while neon, with a filled \(2p\) shell and a small size, is the highest. Arranging in increasing order: \(He\ (48) < Xe\ (77) < Kr\ (96) < Ne\ (116)\), which is option (B).
authoredSolutions.45: Start from 4-nitrotoluene. Bromination: the methyl group is an ortho/para director and the nitro group a meta director; the position ortho to \(-CH_3\) is also meta to \(-NO_2\), so both groups reinforce there and A is 2-bromo-4-nitrotoluene (mono-bromination). \(Sn/HCl\) reduces \(-NO_2\) to \(-NH_2\), giving B. \(NaNO_2/HCl\) at 273-278 K diazotises the amine to the arenediazonium salt C. Hypophosphorous acid \(H_3PO_2/H_2O\) reduces the diazonium group, replacing \(-N_2^{+}\) by \(-H\), so D is 2-bromotoluene. Finally \(KMnO_4/KOH\) followed by \(H_3O^{+}\) oxidises the side-chain methyl to \(-COOH\), giving E = 2-bromobenzoic acid. The option showing A = 2-bromo-4-nitrotoluene and E = 2-bromobenzoic acid is (C). Option (A) wrongly shows dibromination, (B) stops at 2-bromotoluene without side-chain oxidation, and (D) introduces a phenolic \(-OH\) that no reagent in the sequence can install.
authoredSolutions.46: Structures A and B are six-membered (pyranose) rings bearing a \(-CH_2OH\) group and four ring-carbon \(-OH\) groups, i.e. glucopyranoses; C and D are five-membered (furanose) rings carrying TWO \(-CH_2OH\) groups, i.e. fructofuranoses. Within each pair the anomeric carbon fixes the label. In structure A the anomeric \(-OH\) points down (on the same side as the \(C_2\) hydroxyl, trans to the \(-CH_2OH\)), so A is the alpha anomer of glucopyranose, matching (iii); in B the anomeric \(-OH\) points up, so B is the beta anomer, matching (iv). In structure C the anomeric \(C_2\) carries \(-CH_2OH\) up and \(-OH\) down, the alpha-fructofuranose, matching (i); in D the \(-OH\) is up and \(-CH_2OH\) down, the beta-fructofuranose, matching (ii). Hence A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii, option (D).
authoredSolutions.47: In the extraction of copper from copper pyrites the concentrated ore is roasted: \(2Cu_2S + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2Cu_2O + 2SO_2\) and \(2FeS + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2FeO + 2SO_2\), so (A) and (C) do occur. Silica is added as flux and removes the iron(II) oxide as a fusible slag during smelting: \(FeO + SiO_2 \rightarrow FeSiO_3\), so (B) occurs. Reaction (D), \(CaO + SiO_2 \rightarrow CaSiO_3\), is the slag-forming step of the BLAST FURNACE extraction of iron, where limestone is decomposed to lime; lime is not used as the flux in copper extraction (silica is used against the basic FeO instead). Hence (D) does not occur.
authoredSolutions.48: Photochemical smog begins with photodissociation of nitrogen dioxide by sunlight: \(NO_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} NO + [O]\), so \(X = [O]\) (a free oxygen atom) and \(Y = NO\). The highly reactive oxygen atom then combines with molecular oxygen to build up ozone: \([O] + O_2 \rightarrow O_3\), so \(A = O_2\) and \(B = O_3\). This is option (B). Option (A) inverts the roles of \(O_2\) and \(O_3\); (C) and (D) invoke \(N_2O\) and \(N_2O_3\), which are not part of the smog chain.
authoredSolutions.49: P is n-heptane. Step (i) must be aromatisation (catalytic reforming/hydroforming): \(Cr_2O_3\) at 770 K and 20 atm cyclises and dehydrogenates heptane to toluene. Step (ii) is the Etard reaction: chromyl chloride \(CrO_2Cl_2\) followed by \(H_3O^{+}\) oxidises the side-chain methyl selectively to \(-CHO\), giving benzaldehyde. Benzaldehyde has no alpha-hydrogen, so step (iii) with concentrated \(NaOH\) is a Cannizzaro disproportionation, giving sodium benzoate plus benzyl alcohol; step (iv) with \(H_3O^{+}\) liberates benzoic acid. Thus Q = \(PhCOOH\) and R = \(PhCH_2OH\). The sequence \(Cr_2O_3/770\ K/20\ atm\), then \(CrO_2Cl_2/H_3O^{+}\), then \(NaOH\), then \(H_3O^{+}\) is option (C). Option (A) has the first two steps in the wrong order (chromyl chloride cannot act on an alkane), and (B)/(D) use \(KMnO_4\) or \(Mo_2O_3\) as the first step, which will not aromatise heptane cleanly to toluene.
authoredSolutions.50: The clue is the last step: passing the gas/solution into saturated brine gives sodium hydrogen carbonate, which is the Solvay (ammonia-soda) process. Working backwards, C must be ammonium hydrogen carbonate, \(NH_4HCO_3\), because \(NH_4HCO_3 + NaCl \rightarrow NaHCO_3 \downarrow + NH_4Cl\). \(NH_4HCO_3\) is formed from ammonia, water and EXCESS carbon dioxide: \(NH_3 + H_2O + CO_2 \rightarrow NH_4HCO_3\), so B is \(NH_3\). Ammonia is recovered in the Solvay process by treating ammonium chloride with slaked lime: \(Ca(OH)_2 + 2NH_4Cl \rightarrow CaCl_2 + 2NH_3 + 2H_2O\), so A is \(Ca(OH)_2\). Hence A, B, C = \(Ca(OH)_2\), \(NH_3\), \(NH_4HCO_3\), option (D). (Excess \(CO_2\) gives the hydrogen carbonate, not the normal carbonate, ruling out (B) and (C).)
authoredSolutions.51: For a first order reaction the half-life is independent of concentration. After one half-life 50% is left, after two half-lives 25% is left, i.e. 75% is complete. So \(t_{75\%} = 2 \times t_{1/2} = 2 \times 30 = 60\) min. Formally, \(t = \frac{2.303}{k}\log\frac{a}{a-x}\) with \(k = \frac{0.693}{30}\) gives \(t = \frac{2.303 \times 30}{0.693}\log 4 = \frac{2.303 \times 30 \times 2 \times 0.3010}{0.693} = 60\) min.
authoredSolutions.52: In the gaseous (free-ion) state the ions are high spin, so count \(d\) electrons directly. \(V\ (Z=23) = [Ar]3d^34s^2\), so \(V^{3+}\) is \(d^2\) with 2 unpaired electrons, \(\mu = \sqrt{2 \times 4} = 2.83\ BM\). \(Cr\ (Z=24) = [Ar]3d^54s^1\), so \(Cr^{3+}\) is \(d^3\) with 3 unpaired electrons, \(\mu = \sqrt{3 \times 5} = 3.87\ BM\). \(Fe\ (Z=26) = [Ar]3d^64s^2\), so \(Fe^{2+}\) is \(d^6\) with 4 unpaired electrons, \(\mu = \sqrt{4 \times 6} = 4.90\ BM\). \(Ni\ (Z=28) = [Ar]3d^84s^2\), so \(Ni^{3+}\) is \(d^7\) with 3 unpaired electrons, \(\mu = 3.87\ BM\). Only \(Cr^{3+}\) and \(Ni^{3+}\) share a value, so the answer is 2.
authoredSolutions.53: In Carius sulphur estimation all the sulphur of the compound ends up as \(BaSO_4\). Molar mass of \(BaSO_4 = 137 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 233\ u\), of which 32 u is sulphur. Mass of S \(= 1.4439 \times \frac{32}{233} = 0.19831\ g\). Percentage \(= \frac{0.19831}{0.471} \times 100 = 42.1\%\). Nearest integer 42.
authoredSolutions.54: For a dilute solution the van't Hoff osmotic-pressure equation in mass-concentration form is \(\pi = \frac{C}{M}RT\), i.e. \(\frac{\pi}{C} = \frac{RT}{M}\), where \(C\) is in \(g\ L^{-1}\) and \(M\) is the molar mass. The graph supplies \(\frac{\pi}{C} = 6 \times 10^{-4}\ atm/(g\ L^{-1})\). Hence \(M = \frac{RT}{6 \times 10^{-4}} = \frac{0.083 \times 300}{6 \times 10^{-4}} = \frac{24.9}{6 \times 10^{-4}} = 41500\ g\ mol^{-1}\).
authoredSolutions.55: Moles of \(NaOH = 0.025 \times 0.24 = 6 \times 10^{-3}\ mol\). The acid is monobasic, so the same number of moles of acid is needed: \(6 \times 10^{-3}\ mol\), i.e. \(6 \times 10^{-3} \times 24.2 = 0.1452\ g\). With a density of \(1.21\ kg\ L^{-1} = 1210\ g\ L^{-1}\), the required volume is \(\frac{0.1452}{1210} = 1.2 \times 10^{-4}\ L = 0.12\ mL = 12 \times 10^{-2}\ mL\). Hence the answer is 12.
authoredSolutions.56: Energy released by the glucose \(= 1800\ kJ\). Half of it, \(0.50 \times 1800 = 900\ kJ\), is used for the sports activity. The remaining \(900\ kJ\) must be dissipated, otherwise it would be stored; perspiration removes it as the latent heat of vaporisation of water. Moles of water evaporated \(= \frac{900}{45} = 20\ mol\). Mass \(= 20 \times 18 = 360\ g\).
authoredSolutions.57: Count unpaired electrons in each. \(\left[ Ni(CN)_4 \right]^{2-}\): \(Ni^{2+}\ d^8\) with the strong-field \(CN^{-}\) pairs up, \(dsp^2\) square planar, 0 unpaired - diamagnetic. \(\left[ Ni(CO)_4 \right]\): \(Ni(0)\ d^{10}\), \(sp^3\), 0 unpaired - diamagnetic. \(\left[ NiCl_4 \right]^{2-}\): \(Ni^{2+}\ d^8\) with weak-field \(Cl^{-}\), \(sp^3\) tetrahedral, 2 unpaired - paramagnetic. \(\left[ Fe(CN)_6 \right]^{4-}\): \(Fe^{2+}\ d^6\) low spin \(t_{2g}^6\), 0 unpaired - diamagnetic. \(\left[ Cu(NH_3)_4 \right]^{2+}\): \(Cu^{2+}\ d^9\), 1 unpaired - paramagnetic. \(\left[ Fe(CN)_6 \right]^{3-}\): \(Fe^{3+}\ d^5\) low spin \(t_{2g}^5\), 1 unpaired - paramagnetic. \(\left[ Fe(H_2O)_6 \right]^{2+}\): \(Fe^{2+}\ d^6\) high spin \(t_{2g}^4e_g^2\), 4 unpaired - paramagnetic. Paramagnetic species number 4.
authoredSolutions.58: The cell reaction is \(H_2 + 2Fe^{3+} \rightarrow 2H^{+} + 2Fe^{2+}\), with \(n = 2\) and \(E^{o}_{cell} = 0.771 - 0 = 0.771\ V\). The Nernst equation gives \(E = E^{o} - \frac{0.059}{2}\log\frac{[H^{+}]^2[Fe^{2+}]^2}{p_{H_2}[Fe^{3+}]^2}\). With \([H^{+}] = 1\) and \(p_{H_2} = 1\ atm\) this reduces to \(E = 0.771 - 0.059\log\frac{[Fe^{2+}]}{[Fe^{3+}]}\). Substituting \(E = 0.712\ V\): \(0.059\log\frac{[Fe^{2+}]}{[Fe^{3+}]} = 0.771 - 0.712 = 0.059\), so \(\log\frac{[Fe^{2+}]}{[Fe^{3+}]} = 1\) and the ratio is 10.
authoredSolutions.59: Ozone is a resonance hybrid of \(O=\overset{+}{O}-\overset{-}{O}\) and its mirror image. In one canonical structure the central oxygen forms one double and one single bond and carries a positive formal charge, so it has 1 lone pair; the doubly bonded terminal oxygen has 2 lone pairs; the singly bonded terminal oxygen carries a negative formal charge and has 3 lone pairs. Total \(= 1 + 2 + 3 = 6\) lone pairs. (Check by electron count: \(3 \times 6 = 18\) valence electrons; 2 sigma bonds and 1 pi bond use 6, leaving 12 electrons, i.e. 6 lone pairs.)
authoredSolutions.60: The added \(HCl\) converts an equal number of moles of the base to its conjugate acid: \(NH_3 + HCl \rightarrow NH_4Cl\). After adding 0.02 mol \(HCl\), \(n(NH_3) = 0.10 - 0.02 = 0.08\ mol\) and \(n(NH_4^{+}) = 0.10 + 0.02 = 0.12\ mol\) in 1 L. For a basic buffer, \(pOH = pK_b + \log\frac{[salt]}{[base]} = 4.745 + \log\frac{0.12}{0.08} = 4.745 + \log 1.5\). Since \(\log 1.5 = \log 3 - \log 2 = 0.477 - 0.301 = 0.176\), \(pOH = 4.921\) and \(pH = 14 - 4.921 = 9.08 \approx 9\).
authoredSolutions.69: The implication is false only if \(p\land(\sim q)\) is true and \(p\Rightarrow(\sim q)\) is false. But \(p\land(\sim q)\) true forces \(p=T,\ q=F\), and then \(p\Rightarrow(\sim q)=\sim p\vee\sim q=T\). So the statement is never false — it is a tautology.
authoredSolutions.121: \(pH = -\log[H^{+}]\). If the hydrogen ion concentration changes by a factor of 1000, then \(\Delta pH = -\log\left( 10^{3} \right) = -3\) for a thousand-fold INCREASE (and \(+3\) for a thousand-fold decrease). Either way the magnitude of the change is 3 units, and the only option quoting 3 units is (D), a decrease by 3 units, corresponding to the concentration rising a thousand-fold. Options (A) and (C) quote 2 units, and (B) confuses the concentration factor with a pH change.
authoredSolutions.122: The substrate is 2,2,6-trimethylcyclohexan-1-ol. Concentrated \(H_2SO_4\) with heat causes E1 dehydration: protonation of \(-OH\) and loss of water gives a SECONDARY carbocation at C-1. This is flanked by the quaternary C-2 bearing two methyls, so a 1,2-methyl shift from C-2 to C-1 occurs, generating the far more stable TERTIARY carbocation at C-2 while placing a methyl on C-1. Loss of the proton from C-1 then gives the \(C_1=C_2\) alkene, which is TETRASUBSTITUTED (a methyl on each alkene carbon plus both ring bonds) and hence the most stable product, with the third methyl left on the adjacent ring carbon: 1,2,3-trimethylcyclohex-1-ene. That is option (D). Option (C) is the unrearranged elimination product (only trisubstituted, and keeps the gem-dimethyl), (B) is the exocyclic (least substituted) alkene and (A) has the wrong methyl placement.
authoredSolutions.123: Carbon forms two important oxides, \(CO\) and \(CO_2\). Carbon monoxide is a neutral oxide - it forms neither an acid with water nor a salt with base - while carbon dioxide is acidic, giving carbonic acid with water and carbonates with alkali. So Assertion A is correct. The Reason states that \(CO_2\) combines with water in a limited way to form carbonic acid while \(CO\) is sparingly soluble in water; this is factually correct and is exactly why one oxide is acidic and the other behaves as neutral. Both are correct and R correctly explains A, option (C).
authoredSolutions.124: The standard statement is that alkali metals and their salts impart a characteristic colour to an OXIDISING flame, not a reducing flame; the electrons are excited to higher levels by the heat of the flame and emit visible light on returning to the ground state. Assertion A, which specifies the reducing flame, is therefore incorrect. Reason R, that alkali metals can be detected by flame tests, is correct (\(Li\) crimson, \(Na\) yellow, \(K\) violet, \(Rb\) red-violet, \(Cs\) blue). Hence A is not correct but R is correct, option (A).
authoredSolutions.125: In \(K_2Cr_2O_7\) each chromium is in the \(+6\) oxidation state (\(2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6\)). Acting as an oxidant in acidic medium it is reduced according to \(Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^{+} + 6e^{-} \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O\), so chromium ends at \(+3\). The change is therefore from \(+6\) to \(+3\), option (D). (\(Cr^{2+}\), option (C), is only reached by much stronger reduction and is not the dichromate half-reaction.)
authoredSolutions.126: Glyptal, the polyester of ethylene glycol and phthalic acid, is used in paints and lacquers - A matches III. Neoprene, the polymer of chloroprene, resists vegetable and mineral oils and is used for conveyor belts, hoses and gaskets - B matches IV. Acrilan (polyacrylonitrile) is a substitute for wool, used to make synthetic fibres and blankets - C matches II. Low density polythene, being chemically inert, tough but flexible, is used for squeeze bottles, insulation and flexible pipes - D matches I. Hence A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I, option (D).
authoredSolutions.127: Metallic character increases down a group (atomic size increases, ionisation enthalpy falls, so the atom loses electrons more readily) and decreases across a period. Silicon is a metalloid of group 14 and is the least metallic of the four. Beryllium and magnesium are both group 2 metals with \(Mg\) below \(Be\), so \(Be < Mg\). Potassium is a group 1 alkali metal with the lowest ionisation enthalpy of the set and is the most metallic. The increasing order is therefore \(Si < Be < Mg < K\), option (A).
authoredSolutions.128: A cobalt catalyst is used to convert synthesis gas \((CO + H_2)\) into methanol, so A matches IV. Syngas is obtained from coal and steam, \(C(s) + H_2O(g) \rightarrow CO(g) + H_2(g)\), a process called coal gasification, so B matches III. A nickel catalyst is used at about 1270 K in the steam reforming of hydrocarbons, \(CH_4 + H_2O \rightarrow CO + 3H_2\), which produces water gas, so C matches II. Electrolysis of brine solution gives dihydrogen at the cathode and chlorine at the anode, so D matches I. Hence A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I, option (B).
authoredSolutions.129: A larger \(pK_b\) means a weaker base. Aniline is by far the weakest of the four because the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring, so it takes the largest value, \(9.38\) - A matches III.
